 Lakshya Sen vs Loh Kean Yew: Indian Shuttler Faces Stern Test in Hong Kong Open Quarter-Final
 Lakshya Sen vs Loh Kean Yew: Indian Shuttler Faces Stern Test in Hong Kong Open Quarter-Final
 By Romil Shukla View author profile 20 Nov 2026 Badminton Credit Badmintonphoto Like Comment Listen Save Share Lakshya Sen faces Loh Kean Yew in the Hong Kong Open 2026 quarter-finals. Check their head-to-head record, recent form, tactical battle and semi-final implications.
 Lakshya Sen faces a crucial test of his remarkable November resurgence when he takes on Singapore's eighth seed Loh Kean Yew in the men's singles quarter-finals of the LI-NING Hong Kong Open 2026 on Friday.  
 The BWF World Tour Super 500 encounter at Kai Tak Arena promises to be one of the most closely contested matches of the day, bringing together two familiar rivals with contrasting recent journeys. 
 Ranked 11th in the world, Sen enters the quarter-final on the back of an impressive 12-match winning streak, having captured consecutive titles at the Hylo Open and Kumamoto Masters Japan. Loh, currently ranked 12th, arrives with considerable confidence of his own after winning silver at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games, although his campaign in Hong Kong has required considerably more time on court. 
 The match is particularly significant for Sen, who has already secured qualification for the BWF World Tour Finals in Hangzhou. With that objective achieved, the Indian can focus entirely on extending his winning run and making another deep run in a tournament where he finished runner-up last year. 
 The rivalry between the two former training partners has produced 12 senior international encounters, with Sen leading 7-5. However, recent history favours Loh. The Singaporean has won both their meetings in 2026, first at the Badminton Asia Team Championships in February and subsequently at the Asian Games in September. 
 Both encounters went to three games, highlighting Loh's ability to stretch Sen physically and capitalise on crucial passages of play. Their Asian Games meeting was particularly significant, with Loh recovering from an early deficit in the deciding game before producing a decisive scoring burst to secure victory. 
 Interestingly, the opening game could prove decisive once again. In 11 of their 12 previous encounters, the player winning the first game has gone on to win the match. Sen has won all six matches in which he has taken the opening game, while Loh has converted five of his six such opportunities. 
 That statistic makes the opening exchanges particularly important for both players. 
 Sen's current form represents a significant turnaround following a challenging middle portion of the season. After finishing runner-up at the All England Open in March, the Indian struggled to maintain consistency across several international tournaments, suffering early exits at multiple World Tour events. 
 However, November has completely changed the narrative. Sen defeated Jonatan Christie in straight games to win the Hylo Open on November 1 before producing another impressive campaign at the Kumamoto Masters Japan. In the final, he recovered from losing the opening game to defeat Koki Watanabe 13-21, 21-18, 21-14. 
 His Hong Kong campaign has presented different challenges. Sen needed 69 minutes to overcome France's Arnaud Merklé in a demanding three-game opening encounter, saving five consecutive match points before eventually winning 14-21, 21-16, 25-23. 
 He looked considerably sharper in the round of 16, defeating Denmark's Rasmus Gemke 21-11, 21-18 to book his quarter-final place. 
 Playing his third consecutive tournament week, managing physical recovery will remain important. 
 Loh's Comeback Ability Could Be Crucial 
 Loh has not competed since the Asian Games and has entered the Hong Kong Open relatively fresh. Nevertheless, his first two matches have demanded significant physical effort. He began with a three-game victory over Chinese Taipei's Chi Yu-jen, winning 21-23, 21-12, 21-18. He followed that with another comeback against Japan's Kenta Nishimoto, recovering from a 12-21 opening-game defeat to win 21-9, 21-14. 
 Loh has consequently spent 110 minutes on court across six games in Hong Kong. His biggest strength is his ability to generate sudden scoring runs through aggressive attacking badminton. His steep smashes, deceptive drops and quick movement allow him to take control of rallies, particularly when opponents leave short lifts or loose returns. 
 Sen will need to be particularly careful with his defensive positioning and shot selection. 
 The quarter-final is expected to feature high-paced attacking badminton, with both players possessing the ability to dictate rallies. For Sen, the key will be to maintain the defensive discipline that has characterised his recent title-winning performances. Keeping the shuttle deep towards the rear corners, particularly Loh's backhand side, could prevent the Singaporean from establishing his preferred attacking rhythm. 
 Sen must also avoid hurried exchanges and use his placement to create opportunities rather than attempting to match Loh's attacking speed throughout the contest. Loh, meanwhile, will look to replicate the approach that worked against Sen earlier this year. Taking the initiative early, putting pressure on Sen's movement and forcing longer rallies could expose any fatigue accumulated during the Indian's demanding November schedule. 
 There is also an interesting physical dimension to this contest. While Loh has played two three-game matches in Hong Kong, Sen has competed in 13 matches over approximately two and a half weeks. 
 Can Lakshya Extend His Winning Run? 
 Sen enters the contest with confidence, match sharpness and the advantage of having already secured his World Tour Finals qualification. Loh, however, has demonstrated twice this year that he possesses the tactical and physical tools to trouble the Indian. 
 The winner will face either Denmark's third seed Anders Antonsen or Chinese qualifier Zhu Xuanchen in the semi-finals. With several prominent seeds having withdrawn or suffered early exits, the draw has opened up considerably. A victory would put Sen just one match away from another Hong Kong Open final. 
 For the Indian, this is an opportunity to extend his 12-match winning streak, settle the recent score against Loh and continue what has been an outstanding November campaign. But against an opponent who has beaten him twice this year, Sen will need to produce his most complete performance of the tournament.
